source.title: M0.0 — Launch Blocker Discovery: Zero-Surprise MVP Audit & Day-One Dry Run
source.body:
## Early blocker crosscheck (13 Nov)

Use [Persona E2E Scenario Matrix](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/document/shinacare-v1-persona-e2e-scenario-matrix-routine-cod-doorstep-7e8df14cc3da>) to detect missing customer and staff journeys, especially catalog orderability without owned stock and procurement workflow free of supplier login/RFQ. The document is a test plan, not proof of passing tests.

## FULL MVP REQUIREMENTS CROSS-CHECK (13 NOV)

Use [the full MVP feature inventory](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/document/shinacare-v1-full-mvp-feature-inventory-and-gap-audit-source-of-truth-455df701078c>) alongside the 7 launch-blocker areas below. Audit not only missing infrastructure/commerce but **every promised MVP capability**, particularly real chat/recommendations, navigation destinations and after-sales journeys. Include missing-versus-inactive-versus-partial distinction; link findings to current batch tasks.

# First release gate — owner concern, 13 Nov 2026

**Goal:** Discover missing launch dependencies **before** finishing feature tasks, not after. This is an acceptance audit, NOT authorization to redesign or implement extra features. Work can begin in parallel with Git baseline AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#178; do not assign a coding agent yet.

## Questions to prove on current repo / real test data

1. **Catalog/product truth:** available published SKU, exact identity/size, official evidence for usage, INCI/warnings/media, correct public selling price; safe publication/rejection and 404 checks.
2. **Full customer journey:** Arabic mobile Home → concern/category/brand/search → PDP → cart → quote → confirmed address/map pin + service-zone/fee → COD order → tracking, including guest return after browser restart.
3. **Operations:** Order → Admin/Hub consolidated internal Buy List by exact SKU with total unmet quantities → goods acquired manually outside software → internal acquired/shortage marker → Hub pack/hand-off → assigned driver delivery/failed-delivery and COD cash accounting → customer updates. NO supplier login/RFQ/PO/broadcast required.
4. **Business launch decisions:** service-zone map, shipping policy and threshold, pricing/margin exposure, offline purchase sourcing responsibilities and shortage/cancellation fallback, returns/refunds/COD refusal/support contact, required customer-facing policies and owner decisions. Record **explicit owner approval pending** rather than guessing numbers.
5. **Security & data:** real role-scoped auth/IDOR/order ownership, dev bypass disabled, upload/research URL safety, secrets, backups/restore; correct staging vs prod data separation.
6. **External readiness:** actual account/card/credit availability for Railway/Supabase/Cloudinary/OpenRouter/OTP, domain and DNS/TLS, environment variables, storage persistence, migrations and rollback; document constraints and a no-card local/temporary staging alternative.
7. **Integration:** verify actual current HEAD, builds/tests and **attempt a day-one smoke/preview deploy** with a tiny canonical test order and isolated DB; do not defer first deployment attempt until final day.

## Deliverable — launch-blocker register

For every finding: **P0 launch stop / P1 important / P2 defer**, reproduction/evidence, missing owner decision/external dependency, smallest fix, related existing update-batch issue AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#179…307, owner lane **unassigned**, expected verification. Do not duplicate issues unless a confirmed distinct gap cannot be covered. Create a route map + role journey matrix and record which acceptance steps are **not yet verified**. Record failed tests instead of claiming pass.

**Done only when:** audited all 7 categories against repository AND real staging/test assumptions; produced a finite sorted blocker list and evidence of early smoke/deploy attempt or precise access blocker; no unknown dependency silently interpreted as ready. If audit finds P0 blocker, escalate and put it before visual polish/AI. The audit itself does NOT mean launch readiness achieved.

**Owner target:** deploy-ready release candidate 20 Nov 2026; not public production go-live. Three independent coding worktrees, no role assignment yet.

## Added: UI/UX defects are also launch-risk findings (13 Nov owner request)

On **day one**, include a quick visual + functional walkthrough for both Storefront AND Business: Home/Concern/Category/Brand/PLP/PDP/Cart/Checkout/Tracking, Admin/Hub/Driver. Review screenshots and click actual controls at mobile/tablet/desktop widths. Flag broken actions/links, misleading controls, clipped content, high-friction paths, poor hierarchy, unreadable contrast, empty/error states and inconsistent navigation as P0/P1/P2 by **actual impact**, not subjective taste alone. UI implementation belongs to [GLO-303](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-303>); independent acceptance belongs to the final UI gate. A screenshot alone is not functional proof.

## 13 Nov owner scope lock: Full core includes AI

Audit mandatory OpenRouter-backed Chatbot [GLO-301](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-301>) AND Recommendation Engine [GLO-302](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-302>) from day one (API contracts, provider credentials, model access, source/product facts, integration, safety, latency/cost and actual customer UI). Both require evidence before final release approval, not optional post-launch items. Link results to feature coverage [GLO-310](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-310>). Previously postponed or unclear core (e.g. Routine Builder, comparison, reviews) must be surfaced for an explicit decision rather than silently excluded.
